messages:
maria: quick check — thinking about SDK surface for graceful resume + transport retry windows. want to settle on an approach that is ergonomic across py/ts/go without leaking too many knobs. thoughts? :thinking:
kevin: high level: two levers we can expose: resume-token (opaque) + retry-window/backoff policy. keep resume opaque to avoid coupling.
sasha: agree. also consider optimistic resume where client resumes immediately and the SDK transparently falls back to full page fetch if mismatch. that hides complexity from users.
raul: tradeoff: optimistic resume reduces latency for common case but increases server-side work on mismatch. need telemetry to detect mismatch rate. if mismatch > X% fallback to demand-fetch default.
maria: ok — telemetry flag seems reasonable. we should also define default retry window semantics so cross-language libs have same behavior. currently py has 30s, ts 15s, go 20s — chaos.
kevin: propose default: short window for interactive (10s) vs long window for batch (120s) and let callers pick mode: {mode: "interactive" | "batch"}. keep API minimal.
sasha: API sketch: ```js
client.listItems({ mode: 'interactive', resumeToken: 'opaque' })
``` minimal, and SDK docs explain exact retries/backoff.
raul: what about pagination idempotency? if a server returns overlapping items on resume, client dedup should be application-layer. we can provide an optional stable-seq hint header to make dedupe easier.
maria: we shouldn't force application dedupe. can we offer a helper in SDKs (e.g., uniqueById(items)) not on by default.
kevin: yes helper only. also expose a telemetry hook so platform can collect resume success rate and mismatch rate. 
sasha: minor: need a backoff that interacts with transport-level retries (http/gRPC). we should ensure SDK retry window is separate from transport retry (transport deals with transient network errors; resume is about logical continuity). add a small doc blurb in console.
raul: sample config we can normalize across languages: ```json
{"resume_mode":"optimistic","retry_window_seconds":10,"max_backoff_seconds":60}
``` default maps to interactive.
maria: sounds good. last question: should SDK attempt one optimistic resume attempt even if no resumeToken (i.e., client didn't persist)? feels risky.
kevin: no — only resume if token provided. else normal paging. simplicity wins.
raul: agree. one more: add server-side header `X-Resume-Mismatch: 1` so SDK can log and surface a warning to user if mismatch rate spikes.
sasha::+1: also add a CLI/raw log example for ops team.
ci-bot: deploy-checklist: add telemetry metrics: resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, resume_mismatch_count, resume_latency_ms.
maria: ok I'll draft an RFC with the API sketch + default mapping and telemetry fields. will ping for reviews. thanks all :bow:
